# W13 native Codex memory-root candidate

This directory pins source, patch and attribution for the separate native extension selected under David's delegated scope decision. It does not select a Cockpit runtime or install a CLI. Upstream is openai/codex, tag rust-v0.162.1; upstream.json binds its exact source, original license/notice, compiler, patch and candidate executable. Embedded source identifiers are provenance evidence, not reproducible-build or package acceptance.

The pristine reference is third-party/codex-upstream-w13-0.162.1 under the shared repos root. The declared candidate is tools/codex-w13-memory-root, branch codex/w13-memory-root. Upstream push is disabled. Completed patch bytes are checkpointed on the authorized Cockpit branch; no provider fork has been published. Apache-2.0 LICENSE and NOTICE remain verbatim.

`memories.root` selects an explicit absolute base containing existing `memories/` and `memories_v2/` namespaces. Omission preserves native defaults. Account HOME/CODEX_HOME and credential discovery remain unchanged. Dual-write, read/tools, consolidation configuration, status/reset and import destinations use the selected versioned base. A thread's cached namespace does not switch mid-session. Memory job databases need a separate per-binding `sqlite_home`.

The v2 candidate also adds explicit absolute `sqlite_backfill_root` for startup metadata imports. Native startup otherwise backfills every account session into a fresh SQLite database before answering initialization. The optional selector runs normal backfill against only its own sessions/ and archived_sessions/ trees and requires SQLite home separate from account home. It does not fabricate backfill completion, change credentials, redirect native transcript writes or scope all history discovery/background migration/compression. The host must bind/canonicalize roots and review or disable those other tasks. These selectors are not a same-user filesystem sandbox.

Rust 1.95.0 was installed with explicit human approval; the default toolchain is unchanged. The v2 source passes 370 configuration tests, six memory consumer regressions, eight backfill regressions, the separate core backfill/configuration test and generated-schema match. The parser and selected-history cases overlap the focused three-test run; do not double-count them. Native generation/helpers remain off in controlled probes. Real-account memory effects, lifecycle/recovery, production adoption and packaged/installed acceptance remain separate gates.

The adapted diff is patches/0001-isolated-native-memory-root.patch, including normalization of 161 upstream-local Cargo.lock package versions; external lock entries are unchanged. Verify HEAD equals the pinned upstream commit, then use `git apply --check --index --unidiff-zero PATCH` and `git apply --index --unidiff-zero PATCH`. Zero context avoids blank-context-prefix whitespace errors in the containing repository; source and index identity must match.

The unlabelled first build and labelled v1 executable remain preserved in the candidate's target.noindex/preserved tree. Prior receipts retain their frozen source/hash/scope. Current v2 binary build/source/version/hash are recorded in upstream.json after verification. Neither candidate replaces the installed CLI or establishes W13 acceptance.

Live-provider testing found an additional required artifact: codex-code-mode-host. The advertised default model owns code_mode_only, independently of the legacy feature flag, and the CLI-only build cannot execute its memory calls without that companion. David approved its build with Rust 1.95.0. The pinned v8 150.4.0 build failed because its aarch64-apple-darwin prebuilt archive returned HTTP 404; no retry, dependency replacement or source-build fallback was attempted. The companion remains absent. A separately authorized fallback or restored upstream archive is required before live testing can resume. The live harness now requires its pinned hash before any model input; controlled direct-function receipts do not establish code-mode runtime completeness.

`lockSha256` identifies the pristine upstream lockfile; `candidateLockSha256` identifies the checked-in candidate lockfile after local workspace-version normalization. The failed companion build left candidate source, lockfile and CLI bytes unchanged.
